prompt: Two-pipeline application-managed buffer bridge Python app using qimsdk AppSrc and AppSink. Pipeline 1 generates synthetic videotestsrc ball-pattern frames at NV12/1920x1080/30fps into an AppSink with set_buffer_consumer() forwarding buffers. Pipeline 2 receives them via AppSrc (do-timestamp, block, TIME format) and renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Demonstrates cross-pipeline buffer bridging via application code rather than a single linked pipeline.

Audio classification Python app (YAMNet) over an MP4-muxed FLAC track, with the video and a classification label panel composited side-by-side on a Wayland display. qtdemux splits video (h264 decode -> NV12 -> qtivcomposer sink_0) and audio (flacparse -> flacdec -> audioconvert -> audioresample -> audiobuffersplit -> qtimlaconverter feature=lmfe -> qtimltflite(yamnet_float) -> qtimlpostprocess(module=yamnet) -> VideoFilter(RGBA) -> qtivcomposer sink_1). Label panel positioned via composer input(1).set('position',[50,50])/('dimensions',[368,64]).

Audio classification Python app (YAMNet, CPU runtime, no delegate) over an MP4-muxed FLAC track, video plus classification-label overlay composited on a Wayland display. Same topology as the HTP variant but qtimltflite runs on CPU (no external delegate). Audio LMFE features via qtimlaconverter (sample-rate=16000, nfft=96,nhop=160,nmels=64,chunklen=0.96); label panel rendered RGBA into qtivcomposer with list-form pad geometry.

isp-camera preview Python app: captures live frames from the default Qualcomm camera (qtiqmmfsrc), normalizes to NV12/1920x1080/30fps via VideoFilter stream filter, and renders fullscreen on waylandsink with sync disabled for live camera. No AI, no encode, no tee branches. This is the canonical minimal camera-preview shape.

Camera capture encoded to MP4 file Python app, no display, no AI. Captures isp-camera (qtiqmmfsrc) frames at NV12/1920x1080/30fps, encodes via v4l2h264enc (dmabuf io modes), parses H.264, muxes into mp4mux, writes to filesink with eos handling enabled. This is the canonical camera-to-file record shape with no preview branch.

This is the base/canonical single-stage YOLOv8 object detection Python app: qimsdk Pipeline camera app running YOLOv8 detection on frames from the default isp-camera, then displaying results. Captures qtiqmmfsrc camera=0 at NV12/1920x1080/30fps, tees into a qtimlvconverter to qtimltflite (external delegate, htp) to qtimlpostprocess (module=yolov8) branch, merges detection metadata with qtimetamux, overlays boxes via qtivoverlay, renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Explicit-style Element/Pipeline construction with named link() call.

Fused ML-bin YOLOv8 object detection Python app from isp-camera to display, using the single qimsdk MLVideoTFLiteBin wrapper instead of discrete qtimlvconverter/qtimltflite/qtimlpostprocess stages. Captures qtiqmmfsrc camera=0 at NV12/1920x1080/30fps, runs qtimlvideotflitebin (inference-delegate=external, htp, postprocess-module=yolov8) directly in the media path, overlays via qtivoverlay, displays on waylandsink. Use for the compact ML-bin camera detection shape rather than discrete-stage detection.

Two-stage detection-classification daisy-chain Python app: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, Stage 1 runs YOLOX (yolox_w8a8.tflite) object detection on full frames (qtimlpostprocess module=yolov8), then crops detected object ROIs and Stage 2 runs MobileNet-v2 (mobilenet_v2_w8a8.tflite) classification on each ROI (module=mobilenet) via qtimltflite on the HTP/NPU. Overlays both detection boxes and per-ROI classification labels and renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Canonical ROI-based detect-then-classify daisy chain.

Two-stage pose-estimation daisy-chain Python app: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, Stage 1 runs person/foot detection (person_foot_detection_w8a8.tflite, qtimlpostprocess module=qpd) on full frames, then crops person ROIs and Stage 2 runs HRNet pose estimation (hrnetpose_w8a8.tflite, module=hrnet, roi-batch-cumulative mode) on each ROI via qtimltflite on the HTP/NPU. Overlays skeleton keypoints on detected persons and renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Canonical ROI-batch detect-then-pose daisy chain.

Event-triggered recording Python app: run YOLOv8 object detection on an mp4 file, display the overlay, and record the video to /tmp/event-output.mp4 only while a person is present. Dual-pipeline: main pipeline detects (qtimlpostprocess->qtimlmetaparser json->AppSink gate) and tees the overlaid video to a second AppSink (isolated with qtivtransform); a resident recording pipeline (appsrc is-live/do-timestamp/format=TIME fixed NV12 caps -> queue -> v4l2h264enc -> h264parse -> mp4mux -> filesink) is kept PLAYING and fed copied buffers only while the person-presence gate is on. Person detected via object_detection/label JSON keys.

Object detection Python app from mp4-file to display with a custom Python postprocess callback instead of the built-in qtimlpostprocess module. Decodes MP4/H.264 via filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec, tees into a qtimlvconverter to qtimltflite (yolov8 model) branch feeding a qimsdk MLPostprocess element with set_handler() implementing manual tensor decode, NMS, and detection population, merges metadata with qtimetamux, overlays via qtivoverlay, displays on waylandsink. Use when the postprocess decode logic must be hand-written in Python rather than using a built-in module.

Two-stage pose estimation daisy-chain Python app from mp4-file to display: stage 1 person/object detection (qtimltflite, yolov5m model) with a custom Python MLPostprocess callback producing detection boxes, stage 2 HRNet pose estimation (qtimltflite, hrnet_pose model) on stage-1 ROIs with a second custom Python MLPostprocess callback producing keypoints. Both stages use discrete qtimlvconverter/qtimltflite stages, tee/qtimetamux metadata merge per stage, final qtivoverlay renders skeleton keypoints on waylandsink. Use for hand-written pose decode logic instead of a built-in pose postprocess module.

Object detection Python app from mp4-file to display with a custom Python preprocess callback inside the fused ML-bin, using qimsdk MLVideoTFLiteBin.set_preprocess_handler() with preprocess-engine=none instead of a discrete MLVConverter. Decodes MP4/H.264 via filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec, mlbin runs the custom NV12-to-tensor conversion plus yolov8 inference and built-in postprocess, overlays via qtivoverlay, displays on waylandsink. Use for hand-written ML-bin preprocess instead of a discrete external-preprocess pipeline.

Object detection Python app from mp4-file to display with a custom Python preprocess callback replacing the built-in qtimlvconverter tensor conversion. Decodes MP4/H.264 via filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec, tees into a qimsdk MLVConverter (engine=none) with set_handler() implementing manual NV12-to-tensor conversion, feeds qtimltflite (yolov8 model) and the built-in qtimlpostprocess module, merges metadata with qtimetamux, overlays via qtivoverlay, displays on waylandsink. Use when the image-to-tensor conversion math must be hand-written in Python.

Single-stream face detection Python app: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, runs Face Detection Lite (face_det_lite.tflite) inference on full frames via qtimltflite on the HTP/NPU external delegate, decodes detections with qtimlpostprocess, overlays bounding boxes on detected faces, and renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Canonical full-frame face detection shape.

Hand gesture recognition Python app from isp-camera to display: four-stage daisy-chain with palm detection (qtimltflite, palmd module, gpu delegate), qtimetatransform module=roi-palmd for ROI propagation, hand landmark estimation (hlandmark module), gesture embedding (tensor passthrough), and gesture classification (mobilenet module), merged across two qtimetamux stages, overlaid via qtivoverlay onto waylandsink. Explicit-style multi-stage tee/queue wiring named stage_01 through stage_03. Use for the shipped gesture-recognition topology, not a generic N-stage cascade.

Single-stream image classification Python app: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder (qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec), normalizes to NV12, then tees into a display branch and an ML branch. The ML branch runs MobileNet-v2 (mobilenet_v2_w8a8.tflite) classification on full frames via qtimltflite on the HTP/NPU external delegate, decodes the tensor with qtimlpostprocess module=mobilenet, and overlays the top label and confidence via qtimetamux + qtivoverlay before rendering fullscreen on waylandsink. Canonical full-frame classification shape.

YOLOv8 object-detection metadata-parser Python app from an mp4 file: renders the bounding-box overlay on a Wayland display AND taps the raw detection metadata into an AppSink for application-side consumption. Decode -> NV12 -> tee; AI branch qtimlvconverter -> qtimltflite(yolov8_det_w8a8, external HTP) -> qtimlpostprocess(module=yolov8) fans out via a tee: one leg TextFilter->qtimetamux->qtivoverlay->display, the other qtimlmetaparser(module=json)->AppSink whose set_buffer_consumer reads the JSON via Buffer.data().

Two-stage PPE personal protective equipment daisy-chain Python app using fused ML-bin stages from mp4-file to display. Stage 1 person-foot detection using qtimlvideotflitebin with postprocess-module=qpd and model foot_track_net on full frames. Stage 2 PPE gear detection using qtimlvideotflitebin with postprocess-module=yolov8 and model gear_guard_net on stage-1 person ROIs, preprocess-mode=roi-batch-cumulative. Uses v4l2h264dec hardware decode, qtivoverlay renders both stages results, waylandsink fullscreen display. Direct mlbin1 to mlbin2 to overlay to display fused chain, no external tee/metamux metadata branch.

Non-fused ML-bin YOLOv8 object detection Python app from mp4-file to display using qimsdk MLVideoTFLiteBin. Decodes MP4/H.264 via filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec hardware decode with dma io modes, normalizes to NV12, runs qtimlvideotflitebin (inference-delegate=external, htp, postprocess-module=yolov8) directly in the media path, overlays via qtivoverlay, renders on waylandsink fullscreen. File-source variant of the fused ML-bin detection shape.

Monocular depth estimation Python app (MiDaS-v2) with side-by-side comparison on a Wayland display. Decode -> NV12 -> tee; passthrough to qtivcomposer (left pane); AI branch qtimlvconverter -> qtimltflite(midas_v2_w8a8, external HTP) -> qtimlpostprocess(module=midas-v2, labels=monodepth.json colormap) -> VideoFilter(RGBA, no pinned resolution) -> qtivcomposer (right pane). Composer input(N) position/dimensions place the two 960x1080 panes. Depth colormap labels file required.

Canonical multistream Python app: decode one MP4 file into 32 independent simultaneous streams, run non-batched YOLOX object detection on each stream with one qtimlvconverter -> qtimltflite (external HTP/NPU) -> qtimlpostprocess (module=yolov8) chain per stream, overlay bounding boxes, and compose all streams into a dynamic 6x6 grid with qtivcomposer for Wayland display. Supports display as the primary output, with optional MP4 file or RTSP output modes. Uses per-stream queues, qtimetamux/qtivoverlay, composer input(N).set position/dimensions lists, and raises the file-descriptor limit for the high stream count.

Single ISP camera object detection with simultaneous multi-output Python app: captures qtiqmmfsrc camera-0 frames at NV12, runs YOLOv5 (yolov5_float.tflite) detection via qtimltflite on the HTP/NPU external delegate, overlays bounding boxes (qtimlpostprocess module=yolov8), then tees the overlaid stream to THREE simultaneous sinks at once — waylandsink display, an MP4 file (v4l2h264enc + mp4mux + filesink), and an RTSP re-stream (v4l2h264enc + h264parse + qtirtspbin on port 8900). Canonical camera detection with concurrent display+file+RTSP fan-out.

Single-stream object detection to file Python app: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, runs YOLOX (yolox_w8a8.tflite) object detection on full frames via qtimltflite on the HTP/NPU external delegate, decodes detections with qtimlpostprocess module=yolov8, overlays bounding boxes and class labels, then encodes the overlaid video with v4l2h264enc and muxes to an output MP4 filesink. Canonical decode-detect-encode-to-file shape with no display branch.

Parallel inferencing Python app: one decode teed into four independent AI branches composed into a 2x2 grid on a Wayland display. Branch A image classification (mobilenet), B pose (hrnet), C object detection (yolov8/YOLOX), all via qtimlpostprocess->TextFilter->qtimetamux->qtivoverlay; branch D semantic segmentation (deeplab-argmax) rendered RGBA and alpha-blended via its own qtivcomposer. All four tiles feed one top-level qtivcomposer. Because the composers hold tee buffers, each overlay branch's passthrough leg inserts qtivtransform ! NV12 for sole buffer ownership. Composer geometry via input(N).set('position',[x,y])/('dimensions',[w,h]).

Two-stage HRNet pose estimation daisy-chain Python app from an mp4 file to a Wayland display. Stage 1 runs person/foot detection (person_foot_detection_w8a8, module=qpd, qtimlvconverter mode=image-batch-non-cumulative) on full frames; its ROIs feed stage 2 HRNet pose (hrnetpose_w8a8, module=hrnet, qtimlvconverter mode=roi-batch-cumulative). Each stage's text metadata is merged back with its own qtimetamux, then qtivoverlay draws the skeleton keypoints. This detector-cropped cascade is the recommended default for HRNet pose; use full-frame HRNet only when the subject is known to dominate the frame. External HTP/NPU delegate.

MP4 file decode-to-display Python app using qtdemux/h264parse/v4l2h264dec hardware decode, no AI. Reads local mp4-file, demuxes and parses H.264, decodes via hardware v4l2h264dec with dma io modes, normalizes to NV12, renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Uses the start()/wait()/stop() staged lifecycle instead of execute(). This is the canonical multimedia-only file playback shape with no ML/tee/overlay branches.

Single-stream DeepLabV3+ semantic segmentation Python app from an mp4 file, alpha-blended over the original video on a Wayland display. Decode -> NV12 -> tee; passthrough branch to qtivcomposer sink_0; AI branch qtimlvconverter -> qtimltflite(deeplabv3_plus_mobilenet_w8a8, external HTP) -> qtimlpostprocess(module=deeplab-argmax) -> VideoFilter(RGBA, no pinned resolution) -> qtivcomposer sink_1 with alpha=0.5. Rendered mask is RGBA (not BGRA) and unpinned so composer sink-pad dimensions scale it.

Super-resolution Python app (QuickSRNet) with side-by-side comparison on a Wayland display. Decode -> NV12 -> tee; passthrough to qtivcomposer (left, original); AI branch qtimlvconverter -> qtimltflite(quicksrnetlarge_w8a8, external HTP) -> qtimlpostprocess(module=srnet) -> VideoFilter(RGBA, no pinned resolution) -> qtivcomposer (right, upscaled). Composer input(N) position/dimensions define the two panes. Render format is RGBA (srnet emits {RGBA,RGBx}).

Tensor dump / inspection Python app from mp4-file, no display, no postprocess. Decodes MP4/H.264 via filesrc, qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec hardware decode, normalizes to NV12, runs qtimlvconverter to produce a raw model-input tensor (TensorFilter type=UINT8, dimensions 1x520x520x3), writes the tensor buffer to a raw file via multifilesink instead of running inference. Use for capturing/inspecting the exact preprocessed tensor a model would receive, without running qtimltflite.

USB/V4L2 camera preview Python app: captures a live USB UVC webcam via v4l2src with a device-node argument (default /dev/video2), applies qtivtransform, restricts the stream to NV12/1920x1080/30fps via VideoFilter, renders fullscreen on waylandsink with sync disabled. This is the canonical usb-camera preview shape, distinct from the isp-camera qtiqmmfsrc preview app.

Synthetic test video source with string-form StreamFilter caps and geometric transform, Python app to display. Generates videotestsrc ball-pattern frames, applies qtivtransform rotate=180, uses raw caps-string qimsdk StreamFilter objects (video/x-raw,format=NV12,width=1920,height=1080,framerate=30/1 then a resize caps string) instead of the VideoFilter builder, renders on waylandsink fullscreen. Use when raw GStreamer caps strings are needed instead of the typed VideoFilter wrapper.

Runs a QIM SDK Python pipeline entirely from an external YAML configuration file passed as a command-line argument, with no hand-coded topology in main.py. Reads the YAML file into a string, constructs a qimsdk Pipeline directly from the YAML config text via the two-argument Pipeline constructor, and executes it. Use for the YAML-config-driven Python app pattern where the pipeline topology and properties live entirely in an external YAML file rather than being expressed as Element/Pipeline calls.

12-stream batched YOLOv8 object detection Python app: 12 independent MP4 decode chains split into 3 batch groups of 4 streams each. Each group runs qtivtransform(NV12) -> qtibatch -> qtimlvconverter -> qtimltflite(batch-4 model, external HTP, round-robin htp_device_id across cores) -> qtimldemux, with demux outputs linked in the same order as batch inputs. Each stream's per-batch qtimlpostprocess(module=yolov8) RGBA detection layer is composited over that same stream's own original NV12 passthrough at identical position/dimensions -- two interleaved qtivcomposer input pads per stream (passthrough then detection, alpha-blended) -- arranged in a 4x3 grid on waylandsink (sync=False). Raises the file-descriptor limit for the 12 concurrent decode chains.

File based ONNX Runtime (onnxruntime) validation wall Python app comparing YOLOX CPU and QNN HTP detection with DeepLab segmentation and QuickSRNet burst super resolution in a composed MP4 output.

ISP-camera YOLOv8 object detection Python app running inference directly on the QNN runtime (qtimlqnn) against a pre-converted QNN cached-binary model, bypassing the TFLite external-delegate indirection. Captures qtiqmmfsrc camera=0 at NV12/1920x1080/30fps, tees into qtimlvconverter -> qtimlqnn (explicit backend/system shared-library paths, tensors=["boxes","scores","class_idx"] GstValueArray output filter) -> qtimlpostprocess (module=yolov8), merges detection metadata with qtimetamux, overlays boxes via qtivoverlay, renders fullscreen on waylandsink. Use for direct-QNN-runtime detection where the model ships as a cached .bin rather than a .tflite file.

Single-stream face detection Python app, file-to-file: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, runs Face Detection Lite (face_det_lite.dlc) inference on full frames via qtimlsnpe on the SNPE runtime DSP (Hexagon) delegate with an explicit tensors list (heatmap, bbox, landmark required for qfd postprocess caps negotiation), decodes detections with qtimlpostprocess, overlays bounding boxes on detected faces, re-encodes, and writes the result to an output MP4 file via mp4mux/filesink. No display sink.

Three-stage face recognition daisy-chain Python app, file-to-file, all stages on the SNPE runtime DSP (Hexagon) delegate: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, Stage 1 runs Face Detection Lite (face_det_lite.dlc) via qtimlsnpe with an explicit tensors list (heatmap, bbox, landmark) and module=qfd postprocess, Stage 2 runs facial landmark/3DMM alignment (facemap_3dmm.dlc, module=lite-3dmm, roi-batch-cumulative mode) on the Stage 1 ROI, Stage 3 runs face recognition/embedding match (Facial-Attribute-Detection_w8a8.dlc, module=qfr, roi-batch-cumulative) on the Stage 2 aligned ROI. The Stage 3 DLC is a multi-head model whose SNPE default output set emits only the last leaf, so qtimlsnpe sets tensors=[id_feature, liveness_feature, eye_closeness, glasses, mask, sunglasses] to present all six outputs that module=qfr's six-tensor contract requires. Three tee/qtimetamux stages merge each stage's metadata before qtivoverlay; result is re-encoded and written to an output MP4 file via mp4mux/filesink. No display sink. Stage 2 lite-3dmm requires /etc/data/{blendShape,meanFace,shapeBasis}.bin on the device.

Four-stage SNPE/DSP daisy-chain Python app, file-to-file: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, Stage 1 YOLOv8 object detection (yolov8_det_quantized.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, tensors=["boxes","scores","class_idx"], module=yolov8) on full frames; Stage 2 DeepLabV3-Plus-MobileNet semantic segmentation (deeplabv3_plus_mobilenet.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, module=deeplab-argmax) direct-to-qtivcomposer as RGBA mask; Stage 3 HRNet pose estimation (hrnet_pose.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, module=hrnet, roi-batch-cumulative, settings+results mandatory) on Stage 1 ROIs; Stage 4 Inception-v3 classification (inception_v3.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, module=mobilenet) independently on Stage 1 ROIs. Three tee/qtimetamux layers merge Stage 1/3/4 discrete metadata before qtivoverlay; segmentation branch feeds qtivcomposer directly (RGBA render, no qtimetamux). main_split tee shared with qtivcomposer requires qtivtransform+NV12 VideoFilter private-buffer copy on the overlay leg. Result encoded and written to MP4 via v4l2h264enc/mp4mux/filesink. Labels: yolov8.json (Stage 1), deeplab-labels.txt (Stage 2), hrnet.json (Stage 3), classification.txt (Stage 4).

Three-stage face recognition daisy-chain Python app, file-to-file, all stages on the native Qualcomm AI Engine Direct (QNN) runtime loading cached-context .bin models on the HTP/NPU backend via qtimlqnn (backend=/usr/lib/libQnnHtp.so, system=/usr/lib/libQnnSystem.so). Decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, Stage 1 runs Face Detection Lite (face_det_lite_w8a8.bin) via qtimlqnn with an explicit tensors list (heatmap, bbox, landmark) and module=qfd postprocess, Stage 2 runs facial landmark/3DMM alignment (facemap_3dmm_w8a8.bin, module=lite-3dmm, roi-batch-cumulative mode) on the Stage 1 ROI, Stage 3 runs face recognition/embedding match (Facial-Attribute-Detection_w8a8.bin, module=qfr, roi-batch-cumulative) on the Stage 2 aligned ROI. The Stage 3 .bin is a multi-head model whose QNN default output set does not present all six heads, so qtimlqnn sets tensors=[id_feature, liveness_feature, eye_closeness, glasses, mask, sunglasses] to emit all six outputs that module=qfr six-tensor contract requires. Three tee/qtimetamux stages merge each stage metadata before qtivoverlay; result is re-encoded and written to an output MP4 file via mp4mux/filesink. No display sink. This is the qtimlqnn/.bin sibling of the SNPE qtimlsnpe/.dlc variant. Stage 2 lite-3dmm requires /etc/data/{blendShape,meanFace,shapeBasis}.bin on the device.

Three-stage face recognition daisy-chain Python app, file-to-file, all stages on ONNX Runtime (onnxruntime) via qtimlonnx with the CPU execution provider (execution-provider=cpu, optimization-level=disable-all). Decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, Stage 1 runs Face Detection Lite (face-det-lite-w8a8-w8a8.onnx) via qtimlonnx with module=qfd postprocess, Stage 2 runs facial landmark/3DMM alignment (facemap-3dmm-w8a8-w8a8.onnx, module=lite-3dmm, roi-batch-cumulative mode) on the Stage 1 ROI, Stage 3 runs face recognition/embedding match (multi-head model.onnx with external weights in model.data, module=qfr, roi-batch-cumulative) on the Stage 2 aligned ROI. Unlike the SNPE/QNN siblings, qtimlonnx has no tensors= property to filter or reorder outputs, so each model's native ONNX output order must directly satisfy qfd's 3-tensor and qfr's 6-tensor contracts; the CPU execution provider is used because it is built into the ONNX Runtime core and portable, whereas the QNN/HTP ONNX Runtime provider plugin is a separate device install. Three tee/qtimetamux stages merge each stage metadata before qtivoverlay; result is re-encoded and written to an output MP4 file via mp4mux/filesink. No display sink. This is the qtimlonnx/.onnx sibling of the SNPE qtimlsnpe/.dlc and QNN qtimlqnn/.bin variants. The Stage 3 model.onnx needs its model.data external-weights sidecar in the same directory, and the attribute-only face-attrib-net-w8a8-w8a8.onnx must not be substituted for it. Stage 2 lite-3dmm requires /etc/data/{blendShape,meanFace,shapeBasis}.bin on the device.

Python ONNX Runtime (onnxruntime) QuickSRNet Medium super-resolution side-by-side app for MP4 input and fullscreen Wayland display. Uses qtimlonnx CPU with optimization-level=disable-all (the portable generation default; this model additionally fails ONNX Runtime session creation with duplicate node_conv2d node names at higher levels, so disable-all is required here), then srnet RGBA output beside the original video.

Six-stream four-stage SNPE/DSP daisy-chain Python app, file-to-file 3x2 grid: the same MP4 is decoded six times with the Qualcomm hardware decoder, and each of the six streams independently runs the identical four-stage chain - Stage 1 YOLOv8 object detection (yolov8_det_quantized.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, tensors=["boxes","scores","class_idx"], module=yolov8) on full frames; Stage 2 DeepLabV3-Plus-MobileNet semantic segmentation (deeplabv3_plus_mobilenet.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, module=deeplab-argmax) direct-to-qtivcomposer as an RGBA alpha-blended mask; Stage 3 HRNet pose estimation (hrnet_pose.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, module=hrnet, roi-batch-cumulative, settings+results mandatory) on Stage 1 ROIs; Stage 4 Inception-v3 classification (inception_v3.dlc, qtimlsnpe DSP, module=mobilenet) independently on Stage 1 ROIs. Per stream, three tee/qtimetamux layers merge Stage 1/3/4 discrete metadata before a qtivoverlay, the segmentation branch feeds a per-stream qtivcomposer directly, and the main_split tee shared with that composer requires a qtivtransform+NV12 private-buffer copy on the overlay leg. The six per-stream composited NV12 outputs are tiled into a 3x2 grid (640x540 cells, 1920x1080 canvas) by a final qtivcomposer using per-pad position/dimensions, then encoded once and written to a single MP4 via v4l2h264enc/mp4mux/filesink. Built by looping the verified single-stream topology six times with index-suffixed element names. Heavy stress topology: 24 concurrent DSP inferences plus six decode legs and one encode leg. Labels: yolov8.json, deeplab-labels.txt, hrnet.json, classification.txt.

Single-stage image classification Python app, file-to-file: decodes an MP4 file with the Qualcomm hardware decoder (qtdemux, h264parse, v4l2h264dec), normalizes to NV12, then tees into a passthrough video leg and a classification leg. The classification leg runs Inception-v3 (inception_v3.onnx) on ONNX Runtime (onnxruntime) via qtimlonnx with the CPU execution provider (execution-provider=cpu, optimization-level=disable-all), decodes the tensor with qtimlpostprocess module=mobilenet, and the top label is merged back via TextFilter + qtimetamux and drawn with qtivoverlay. The annotated stream is hardware-encoded (v4l2h264enc) and written to one output MP4 via h264parse/mp4mux/filesink. The CPU execution provider is built into the ONNX Runtime core and portable, unlike the QNN/HTP provider plugin; optimization-level=disable-all keeps Transpose nodes intact for qtimlonnx layout/caps negotiation; qtimlonnx has no tensors= property so the native ONNX output order must satisfy the module=mobilenet contract. CPU inference runs below realtime, so pipeline.eos(True) and a natural-EOS drain are required for mp4mux to finalize a playable file. This is the ONNX-CPU file-to-file sibling of the TFLite/HTP display classification app.

Six-stream HRNet pose estimation Python app, file-to-file 3x2 grid, running HRNet (hrnet_pose_w8a8.bin) directly on the full decoded frame of six independent decode instances of the same MP4 via qtimlqnn (QNN native cached .bin runtime, backend=/usr/lib/libQnnHtp.so, system=/usr/lib/libQnnSystem.so) - no detection/ROI-crop stage. Per stream qtimlpostprocess module=hrnet (results=2, labels=hrnet.json, settings=hrnet_settings.json) decodes keypoints, a tee/qtimetamux pair merges pose metadata back onto the video path, and qtivoverlay draws the skeleton. All six overlaid NV12 outputs are tiled into a single 3x2 grid (640x360 cells) by one shared qtivcomposer, hardware-encoded (v4l2h264enc), muxed and written to one output MP4. This HRNet QNN cached-binary model exports a single native output tensor, so qtimlqnn carries no tensors= filter (unlike the multi-tensor YOLOv8 QNN model). High-concurrency topology (six decode legs + six concurrent HTP inferences); raise the device file-descriptor limit. Full-frame native-QNN .bin variant; the previously cached HRNet reference is the TFLite+QNN-delegate cascade.
